name: Critical minerals
value: US gallium ban pause ended 27 Nov; licences stay
summary: China's one-year pause of its gallium, germanium and antimony ban on the US reached its 27 Nov end; licensing stays
state: China's suspension of its ban on gallium, germanium and antimony exports to the US, which took effect on 9 Nov 2025, ran until 27 Nov 2026 (The Star), after which the ban could return; licensing requirements for these metals were not lifted by the pause. On 9 Nov China extended a separate suspension of controls on five rare earths to 10 Jan 2027, but April 2025 controls on seven rare earths remain in force (S&P Global). Searches on 28 Nov found no announcement on the gallium pause and no production stoppages outside China linked to export bans, so Watch holds.
for_you: Makers of chips, defence electronics, batteries and magnets that rely on Chinese gallium, germanium, antimony or rare earths are most exposed; licensing delays tend to show up first as longer lead times and higher prices.
rubric_hit: Licensing regime in force and US ban pause at its 27 Nov end: Watch; no reported stoppages outside China for Alert

sources.title: The Star — China suspends ban on exports of gallium, germanium, antimony to US

why: Rare earths, gallium, germanium and graphite are chokepoints for chips, EVs and defence — and China dominates processing.
drivers: Export controls, trade disputes, mine outages, stockpiling.

rubric.alert: Export bans in force that are causing reported production stoppages outside China.
rubric.watch: New export controls announced or licensing slowed.
rubric.normal: No new export restrictions in the past month.
